Hi Samantha / Raj —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation I put together a concise closure roadmap that aligns legal review (MSA + DPA) with procurement timing and your internal GDPR review windows. The goal is to land a signed MSA + DPA and an executed order form within a four-week horizon, with clear handoffs for procurement and security.

I've attached a one-page MAP (Aurora_MAP_v1.pdf) and a draft order form workbook. High-level proposed sequencing: 

- Day 0: Redwood provides final MSA + DPA drafts (attached DPA template) and order form draft.
- Day 2–7: Aurora legal / security review. Rapid questions routed to Marissa (cc'd).
- Day 7–12: Commercial review & PO processing (Aurora procurement team).
- Day 12–18: DocuSign routing (MSA + DPA) and countersign.
- Day 18–28: Implementation kickoff + provisioning (post-signature tasks).

Open items for us to confirm:
1) Which internal Aurora stakeholders own procurement/PO issuance? (Raj?)
2) Any mandatory vendor assessments / SOC 2 evidence you need before countersign?
3) Do you require any redlines to the DPA that would block a two-week legal review window?

Next steps: Samantha, can you confirm your procurement lead and a target PO date? Marissa, can you review the attached DPA and flag anything non-standard for Aurora? Neha, please coordinate the hubspot deal timeline and the docusign flow if legal approves.

Thanks — aim to keep this tight so we don't miss their Q4 pilot window.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear plan and the one-pager. Quick answers:
- Procurement owner: Raj Patel (cc'd) will own the PO. Target is to issue PO by Sep 14 if legal sign-off is clean.
- Security evidence: Our InfoSec team usually wants a SOC 2 summary + encryption details. Can Marissa upload a short evidence bundle (SOC 2 summary, hosting region, KMS details)? If not immediately available, a plan to provide those docs by Sep 6 would work.
- DPA redlines: We try to avoid custom DPA terms, but we do have two standard asks: 1) data subprocessing disclosure, and 2) a 30-day notification window for breaches.

If you can confirm those two items are acceptable or call them out now, we can keep legal on a 5–7 business day review cadence.

Thanks — Samantha
